answers.answer: 1) Four players use 3 randomly selected Pods. 2) Put lowest-numbered in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all begin Locked side up. 3) Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total at 4 players).

1) Remove Corporate and Personal Objectives showing a higher player count than actual; shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player one of each, hidden. 2) Players choose one of their two at the First Encounter, when the first Intruder miniature appears, before resolving that Encounter; each removes the rejected card face down without looking at others' rejects. 3) Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger the choice. The summary does not separately specify disposition of the unchosen one at initial deal, but at First Encounter it is removed from game.

1) Discard the used Action card plus exactly 2 other Action cards from hand to pay its printed cost 2. 2) Contamination cards cannot pay Action costs. 3) For sections separated by OR, choose one effect; discard the card used and pay the required additional Action cards for that action.

answers.answer: 1) Fire wound occurs when the Character ends their own round in the burning Room, after their actions (1 Light Wound each such round). 2) Passing ends their normal Actions for the Player Phase; no acting again. 3) When passing, may discard any number of hand cards. 4) Fire is checked at the end of a Character's round, not during later players' rounds; if the Character had another round before passing, each round ending there causes a wound. Passing players take it once at end of their round and no more that turn.

1) On entry to unexplored Room, flip tile, set its Item count by rotating tile to align token number to board counter, resolve Exploration effect, then remove token to box. 2) If Room is empty, roll Noise and place result's marker in the indicated Corridor; an Intruder destination can cause Encounter. 3) Silence means no Noise roll. 4) Danger means no Noise roll: all eligible neighboring Intruders move in; if none eligible, place Noise in every unmarked connected Corridor. 5) If destination already has any Character or Intruder, do not make the ordinary Noise roll. 6) Slime turns Silence into Danger.

1) Costs 2 Action cards; otherwise follows normal movement rules and places a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to destination instead of a Noise roll. 2) Forbidden in Combat, or if every Corridor connected to destination already has Noise. 3) Closed Door blocks crossing. 4) A miniature cannot stop in Corridor; it must enter a Room.

(A preexisting Corridor Noise marker ordinarily triggers Encounter instead of placing a second.)

1) Danger moves ALL neighboring Intruders not in Combat into the Room. 2) If none are eligible, place Noise markers in all connected Corridors lacking one. 3) Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it creates Combat. 4) Slime makes Silence resolve as Danger.

1) During Encounter, Blank places a Noise marker in every connected Corridor, adds an Adult to bag only if it was last token and an Adult is available, returns Blank to bag; no miniature appears. 2) In bag development, Blank adds one available Adult (if none available, none); then returns Blank to bag. No Noise instruction applies to that development branch.

1) Attempting 9th Fire or Malfunction marker ends game/ship explodes; if marker already in target Room, extra placement does nothing (max one per Room). 2) Discarded markers return to their pool. 3) Ship loss of hull integrity kills all Characters aboard including hibernating, and everything else aboard including Intruders.
